heard: a city-bus-sized asteroid snuck halfway inside our moon's protective orbit without warning. In February 2023, astronomers using a Canary Islands telescope spotted the unexpected cosmic visitor. Detailed measurements revealed the rocky visitor was between 40 and 90 meters across. Worse still, early math briefly listed it as a virtual impactor for March 2026. Further tracking thankfully ruled out the collision, dropping the rock from the risk table completely. On March 25, the asteroid roared past at a distance of 175,000 kilometers. Amateur stargazers easily spotted the fast cosmic visitor using small backyard telescopes. A city-bus-sized asteroid snuck halfway inside our moon's protective orbit.
